sections.overview: This geometrid moth is a cool-region species recorded from European mountain systems and farther across northern Eurasia.
sections.identification: Its dark forewings contrast with nearly white hindwings, giving the flying moth a striking black-and-white appearance.
sections.habitat: It is associated with mountain forests, alpine meadows and cool streamside vegetation.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on bedstraws, especially Galium palustre, a host plant listed by several European references.
sections.behavior: Adults fly mainly in early summer and may be flushed by day or attracted to light at night.
sections.reproduction: Larvae are reported to overwinter, but references do not establish a consistent number of generations across the range.
sections.ecology: Several geographic forms are recognized, including Pyrenean and northern forms; local identification should account for this variation.
sections.conservation: French records are concentrated in the Alps and Pyrenees, but no verified global threat category was found.
